clue.text: Light opera featuring "Drink! Drink! Drink!"

indicators.note: a phrase featuring something has it inside, so the answer sits within the words light opera

explanation.surface: A comic operetta includes a rousing drinking chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' says the letters sit inside 'Light opera', across the join of the two words. The triple exclamation defines a verb meaning to drink repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is to drink alcohol habitually and heavily, which the repeated command evokes.

clue.text: Roman historian's account accepted by emperor

definitions.note: read as 'Roman historian is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: something accepted by a person is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Titus was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A Roman chronicler's version of events is endorsed by the ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'historian' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus wrote the Annals and Histories, chronicling the early Roman Empire.

clue.text: Plan soldiers put together, one used for screening purposes

parts.note: a plan or scheme is a project
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops combine a scheme with a device for showing films.
explanation.definitionFit: A projector throws images onto a screen, so its purpose is screening films.

clue.text: Daughter is funny about American nightclub phenomenon

indicators.note: one piece about another goes round it, so the second sits inside

parts.note: a funny person or thing is comic

explanation.surface: A girl is amused by a craze from US clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' looks like a description of the daughter, but it supplies a word that 'about' wraps round the American abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco music was the dance-floor craze of 1970s nightclubs.

clue.text: During first part of dinner I turn blue

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter here

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Someone goes blue in the face as dinner begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep shade of blue, between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Henry forsakes friend, composer from north of England

indicators.note: the letter for Henry forsakes, or leaves, the word for friend

parts.note: a chum is a friend
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Havergal Brian was an English composer

explanation.surface: A man named Henry abandons his musician pal from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forsakes' removes H from CHUM to leave CUM. Cumbria is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cumbrian comes from Cumbria, the county in England's far north-west.

clue.text: False ideas unmarried girl's got about the first stage of pregnancy

indicators.note: one piece about another goes round it, so the second sits within

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried girl; 's here is 'has', linking
conception is the moment pregnancy starts

explanation.surface: A single woman has mistaken beliefs about early pregnancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the girl's title round the pregnancy stage, so its last letter lands at the end; the 's after 'girl' is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Misconceptions are mistaken beliefs or wrong notions.

clue.text: Novelist dwelling in Kent area

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE
a hut is a simple dwelling

explanation.surface: A writer lives in a corner of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Nevil Shute wrote A Town Like Alice and On the Beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevil Shute was an English-Australian author of popular novels.

clue.text: Dock one dog after another

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to tail someone is to follow after another person

explanation.surface: One hound follows another into the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock is to cut short, as a tail is docked, so it means to curtail.

clue.text: Join rebellion during work, in a manner showing initiative

parts.note: to join a race or club is to enter it

indicators.note: one thing during another sits within it

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
a rising is a rebellion

explanation.surface: Someone joins a revolt at work, showing enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places the rebellion word inside the work word; the whole definition is an adverb phrase, matching the -LY ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting enterprisingly means acting with initiative and resourcefulness.

clue.text: One has nothing to lose, entering mass with wreath on head

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a crowd is a mass of people

indicators.note: the word loses a letter, here the round zero

parts.note: taken as the word one
O, the round zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone with nothing to lose joins the throng in a garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' drops O from ONE, leaving NE; 'entering' puts NE in CROWD.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowned means having a crown or garland placed upon the head.

clue.text: Square dancing by male entertainer

indicators.note: letters dancing move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man joins a square dance as performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square dancing' reads as a folk dance, but 'dancing' is the anagram signal and 'by' just means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquer is a performer in a masque, a courtly entertainment.

clue.text: Gay entertainment with appealing character?

parts.note: John Gay wrote a ballad opera; its characters are mendicants who make appeals for alms

explanation.surface: A cheerful show has a charming lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is the 18th-century dramatist John Gay, not a mood; 'appealing' means begging rather than attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's 1728 ballad opera is about thieves and beggars, characters who appeal for charity.

clue.text: Place one back on board for exercises

annotationWithheld.why: Place one back on board for exercises: the parse puts rev(PUT+I) inside SS, but 'on board' must both supply SS (steamship) and signal the container, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Place one back on board for exercises

clue.text: Absurd, sending servicemen back to islands near California?

indicators.note: sending them back reverses the order of the letters

parts.note: RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a body of servicemen
CI is the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Posting airmen to islands off California would be ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending ... back' reverses the servicemen; 'near' merely puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something farcical is ridiculous, like the improbable action of a farce.

clue.text: Make arrangement with Conservative Check tod personality

annotationWithheld.clue: Make arrangement with Conservative Check tod personality

clue.text: Richard Murphy said to be a tyrant

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken, so the sound matters

parts.note: Dick is short for Richard, and a murphy is slang for a potato, a tater

explanation.surface: A man called Richard Murphy is reputed to be despotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' is not a surname but slang for potato (from its Irish association), so 'Dick tater' when spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator is an absolute ruler, a tyrant.

clue.text: Island offers endless fish: wonderful to return

indicators.note: endless means losing its final letter

parts.note: a sardine is a small fish

indicators.note: the letters return, reading backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written as AI

explanation.surface: An island provides a non-stop supply of fish, glorious to come back to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts SARDINE to SARDIN; 'to return' turns AI to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is a large Mediterranean island belonging to Italy.

clue.text: Mule perhaps located source of marijuana in purest form

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it
in another form means rearranged
the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone finds the purest grade of cannabis on a drug runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges PUREST, with M (from 'source of marijuana') put inside; 'located' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sumpter is a pack animal, such as a mule or horse carrying baggage.

clue.text: Writer engaged by publishing company to speak more freely

indicators.note: someone engaged by a firm is taken inside it

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author signs with a publisher so they can be frank.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to talk more candidly and freely.

clue.text: Pockets gratuity picked up in period of service?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pocket a ball in snooker is to pot it
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A waiter pockets a tip in the middle of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses POTSTIP as a whole. A pit stop is when a racing car is serviced.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is the pause in a motor race when a car is refuelled and serviced.

clue.text: Wrongly assume he's an Irishman?

indicators.note: wrongly put means set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Don't take it for granted that he comes from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he's' links; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamus is a typical Irish man's name, so the example fits.

clue.text: Communist vote secured by minister Stalin corrupted

indicators.note: held fast inside the other piece
corrupted signals the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: X is the mark placed on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A Communist ballot was rigged by a corrupted Stalin aide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges the fodder words, and 'secured by' places the voting mark within them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist-Leninist follows the communist doctrine of Marx and Lenin.

clue.text: Vital organ's actual name is concealed

definitions.note: means of a kidney, an adjective

indicators.note: the short piece is concealed inside the longer word

parts.note: real means actual

explanation.surface: A kidney's true title is kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, which are vital organs.

clue.text: Tense about performing this evening

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it

parts.note: tight means tense
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: Nerves before tonight's show.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the present or coming evening.

clue.text: An old enemy pinpointed in mountain search

indicators.note: located precisely inside, so the pieces go within

parts.note: MT is the abbreviation for mount or mountain
Hun was a derogatory name for the German foe of the World Wars

explanation.surface: A former foe is located on a peak after a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhunt is an organised search for a person.

clue.text: Get better pass from the wings — it's driven in competitively

parts.note: to rally is to recover or improve
in football a cross is a pass from the wing into the middle

explanation.surface: A player recovers and sends the ball in from the flank.
explanation.walkthrough: Football language misleads; rallycross is a motor sport on mixed surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallycross is a motor sport raced on mixed tarmac and dirt circuits.

clue.text: Page worker in van … making this sound?

indicators.note: in the van means at the front, so this piece leads

parts.note: a worker is a bee

explanation.surface: A pager beeps at a worker in a delivery vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is not a vehicle but the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A beep is the short electronic sound a pager makes.
